findings.summary:
I ran the collaboration module the way two people would use it, on a private bench: a private Postgres 16 cluster, the state service (services/state-api), a two-user fake git host (org team, repo team/shared) and two daemons, each with its own UI (Ada: 48774/2374, Bob: 48775/2375). The model was the stand-in (--provider bench). Bob's daemon reached Postgres through a TCP proxy, so I could cut his connection on its own. I walked all 7 journeys through the UI with Playwright: 124 screenshots under /tmp/frbench/collab/walk/steps/{ada,bob,bobnaive}/.

What works:
- Claim-before-work stopped double work every time. Skips were recorded as held_by / not_claimable, and the agents sent each other "...you hold the claim; I moved on."
- Agent-to-agent handoffs get delivered, read and acted-on receipts, and an unacknowledged handoff comes back at the sender's next session.
- On the repository project, Bob's agent noticed it would touch the same file as Ada's agent and warned her agent.
- The schema sync gate pauses and resumes correctly.
- Private memory and the vault stayed on each PC.

The module is not usable for two real people yet:
- **Joining:** joining a shared store has no app or setup-guide path. A second install with no email selector silently becomes the first person; the setup assistant even renames her.
- **Sharing:** sharing a project needs the other person's raw database id, typed as a command in chat.
- **Visibility:** every project on the store is visible to, and writable by, every install, shared or not.
- **One-sided:** sharing works in one direction only. The project owner never gets peers, handoffs, overlap checks or change messages from the joiner.
- **No messaging:** nothing in the app lets a person send a message to the other person or their agent.
- **No live updates:** nothing reaches the other desktop live, and there is no polling fallback either.
- **No-repo projects:** a shared project without a repository splits into two diverging folders, while both screens say the work is done.
- **Network drop:** a network drop mid-session leaves a phantom "running" session. It blocks Start on both PCs and refuses that agent's next session. Only a daemon restart clears it.
- **Repository creation:** "Create the repository" on a shared project puts it in the presser's private account. The other person's next session then fails with a raw 404.
- **Privacy:** Ada's private chat is stored in the shared database, and Bob's app showed it with Ada's lines labelled "You:".

Findings: 15 major, 7 minor, 2 polish.

findings.title: A second install with no selector becomes the first person; the setup assistant then renames her
findings.what_a_person_meets: Bob points his fresh install at the shared store (FORERUNNER_STATE_URL) and opens the app. 'Your name' is prefilled with 'Ada'. He types 'Bob' and continues. From then on his app runs as Ada with her agent Alice, her cap and her Inbox, and Ada's name in the shared store is now 'Bob'.
findings.evidence: identity.ts:183-186: a store holding exactly one human binds that human as 'only' when no selector is given. Daemon log of the test install: 'install identity {humanId: 01a19dee-…(Ada), source: "only"}', and 'runtime composed … human: Ada, agent: Alice'. Screenshot steps/bobnaive/01-naive-bob-setup-welcome.png: name field value "Ada". After Continue, the copied store's human row read name='Bob' for Ada's id. ADR 0082's Consequences say an install without a selector is refused; that is only true once the store holds 2 or more humans.
findings.expected: A store that already holds another person never binds a new install without an explicit selector. The app asks 'Are you <name>, or are you joining?' and creates the joiner's own human.
findings.fix_hint: In lookupInstallHuman, on a non-sqlite or shared store with humans>=1, an install that has no config.json humanId and no email gets 'none/ask' instead of 'only'. Add a 'Join a shared project' step in the setup assistant that records humanEmail. Never let /setup/profile rename a human this install did not create.

findings.title: No path in the app or the person docs to join a shared store; the guide's 'point both installs at the state service' does not share anything
findings.what_a_person_meets: The owner follows the setup guide, sets FORERUNNER_STATE_API_URL and saves the admin token. Settings then says 'This PC uses the state service', but both PCs still work on their own local SQLite and nothing is shared. The only working path is an undocumented FORERUNNER_STATE_URL holding Postgres credentials, plus `fr setup --email --state-url`, which the installed app does not have (U-050).
findings.evidence: compose.ts:1264-1268: the store comes from FORERUNNER_STATE_URL or config.stateUrl only. compose.ts:3563-3567: FORERUNNER_STATE_API_URL is used only for Settings → Devices. grep: FORERUNNER_STATE_URL appears in neither docs/setup-guide.md nor docs/user-guide.md. setup-guide.md:339-341 says the shared state 'lives in the state service you point both installs at'. The setup assistant has only Welcome/Claude/GitHub/Done (steps/ada/01-09). Bob had to run `fr setup --non-interactive --email bob@example.test --state-url postgres://…` before his first start.
findings.expected: A person-level 'Work with someone' flow: Settings or the setup assistant takes the shared address and the person's email, checks it, records humanEmail, and restarts. The user guide describes it.
findings.fix_hint: Add a Settings → Sharing section and a setup-assistant step that write stateUrl and humanEmail through runSetup. Decide whether desktops keep direct Postgres access (ADR 0024) or go through the service; then fix the setup-guide wording.

findings.title: Sharing a project needs the other person's database id typed as a chat command
findings.requirement: F (membership), design: one place per setting
findings.what_a_person_meets: Ada wants Bob on 'Team site'. The New project dialog has no people field, and Settings → per project has no sharing row. Saying 'share this project with Bob (bob@example.test)' in chat does nothing. It works only with `tool: settings_set {"key":"shared_with","value":["01a19df1-…"]}`, which shows a card reading `["01a19df1-4653-…"]` and needs Inbox → Details → 'approve on device'. No screen shows Bob's id; I took it from the database.
findings.evidence: settings-view.ts:152-245: the project rows have no shared_with or members row. commands/settings.ts:238-246 defines shared_with as raw human ids. steps/ada/11 (dialog), 16 (Advanced, no sharing row), 19 (words ignored), 21-25 (tool line, raw-id card, 'Not done: a chat or email yes alone is not enough', approve on device). The chat context the stand-in reported lists facts 'now, active_project, unread_messages, open_requests, running_sessions' and no people. Step count for Ada: 3 actions plus 1 impossible lookup.
findings.expected: 'Share' on the project page: pick a person by name or email, one confirmation, and the other person sees the project and an Inbox line saying who shared it.
findings.fix_hint: Add a people picker over store.human (name, email) and a project 'People' section. Write members (agent ids) and shared_with together. Render names, never ids, in change cards.

findings.title: Every project on the store is visible to, and writable by, every install, shared or not
findings.what_a_person_meets: Ada creates 'Shared app' and shares it with nobody. Bob's Home lists it at once. Bob can open it, add a task (201) and start sessions on it. Only its Files tab and Note box answer 'not your project / Retry'.
findings.evidence: server.ts:861-863: GET /projects returns store.project.active() with no ownsProject filter. ownsProject is enforced only in docs-routes.ts:200/254/283/295/307, queue-routes.ts:50/77 and server.ts:2515 (speak). Bob's POST /projects/01a19e0c…/tasks was answered 201 on the unshared project (steps/bob/55-bob-sees-unshared-project.png, 54-bob-home-check). steps/bob/63-bob-j7-overview-prs.txt shows 'not your project / Retry' twice next to a Last result of work his own agent did.
findings.expected: An install lists and acts only on projects whose members or shared_with include its human. One rule applies on every route, so no screen shows a 403 banner on a project the person can otherwise use.
findings.fix_hint: Filter /projects, /projects/:id/*, /tasks/*, /sessions and /chat by ownsProject. Add a route test where a second human on the same store sees nothing unshared.

findings.title: Sharing is one-sided: the owner gets no peers, handoffs, overlap checks or change messages from the joiner
findings.what_a_person_meets: After sharing, Bob's Overview shows Peers (Ada's agent). Ada's Overview never shows a Peers section, although Bob's agent did 6 tasks on her project. Her agent never sends Bob a handoff and never checks overlap with Bob's work. When Bob adds tasks or changes settings, Ada gets no Inbox line.
findings.evidence: create-project.ts:64 sets members=[creator's agent]. runner.ts:3139-3153 (defaultPeers) uses members when set, so Ada's agent has no peers. Every Ada session logged peers.feed {"peers": []}, while Bob's listed Ada's agent. GET /projects/:id/peers returned peers:[] for Ada and Ada's agent for Bob. Messages: handoffs from Bob's agent to Ada's agent; none from Ada's agent to Bob's. executor.ts:664-672 sends change sentences only to shared_with humans other than the actor, so Ada (in members, not in shared_with) got nothing for Bob's 'Add a footer…' task or his budget change.
findings.expected: Membership is one list of people. Both agents are peers of each other, both send handoffs, both run overlap checks, and both people get each other's change sentences.
findings.fix_hint: Derive peers from members ∪ the principals of shared_with humans ∪ the author. Send change sentences to every member human except the actor. Cover both directions in a test.

findings.title: A shared project without a repository splits into two diverging folders while both screens say done
findings.what_a_person_meets: Bob's Overview says 'Done: all 5 tasks', but his Files tab says 'Nothing written yet'. Later his agent 'adds a footer to index.html' in its own nearly empty folder, without Ada's styles.css or script.js. Ada's Overview lists 'Changed by the last session: notes/coder-rename-the-footer-link.md', which is not on her PC, and clicking it shows her folder without it.
findings.evidence: Bob's workspace held .git, .gitignore, docs and a fresh index.html. Ada's held README.md, checks/, docs, index.html, script.js and styles.css (ls of both <home>/data/projects/01a19df2…/workspace). Screenshots: steps/bob/12-bob-overview-after-ada-session.png, 13-bob-files-after-ada.png, 19-bob-after-both-start.txt ('Your files … Changed by the last session: index.html, script.js, styles.css …' under Bob's own path), steps/ada/31-ada-overview-after-bob-handoff.png, 32-ada-opens-bobs-file.png.
findings.expected: A project without a repository cannot be shared, or sharing it first requires creating a shared repository. 'Your files' never lists files that are not in that folder.
findings.fix_hint: Refuse shared_with on a project with repos=[] and offer 'Create a repository' first. Filter 'Changed by the last session' to sessions of this install.

findings.title: Running chip, Stop all and 'Open running session' count the other person's sessions
findings.requirement: Design §3.1 (Stop all, running chip), user guide 'Kill switch'
findings.what_a_person_meets: While Ada's agent works, Bob's header reads 'Alice is working on "Check that…" · Stop all (1 running)'. His project page offers only 'Open running session' (Ada's), so he cannot press Start. Stop all on his PC stops nothing of Ada's. With both agents running, each side shows a single 'Working now' line.
findings.evidence: project-status.ts:318-345 (workingOn) takes any working session on the project, whatever its agent. ProjectPage.tsx:118-128 replaces Start with the link. ShellBars.tsx:20-22 and 111 count it. Screenshots: steps/bob/11-bob-overview-now.txt, 19-bob-after-both-start.txt, steps/ada/27-ada-after-both-start.txt. The user guide (line 555) says the other person's sessions keep running.
findings.expected: The chip and Stop all count this install's sessions only. The project page shows 'Ada's agent is working on X' as information and still offers Start.
findings.fix_hint: Return working sessions per agent with owner names. Filter the chip and Stop all to rt.human's agents. Keep Start visible when only a peer works.

findings.title: A network drop mid-session leaves a phantom running session that blocks both PCs until a restart
findings.what_a_person_meets: Bob's PC loses the database for about a minute during a task. Afterwards both apps say 'Alice is working on "Write a contributors list…" · 2 min' forever. Stop all shows 'Sessions are stopped' while the chip still says working. Neither project page offers Start. Bob's next start says 'Alice is already working in another session, so this one did not start.' The task is released only when Bob's daemon restarts, and recovery then says 'Interrupted: Forerunner closed while this session ran.', which is untrue.
findings.evidence: Bob's daemon.log: 'session failed {sessionId 01a19e08-ad9f…, connect ECONNREFUSED}' and 'release failed'. The session row stayed status 'running' after reconnect, after a restart while sync was paused, and after Stop all. POST /sessions answered 409 conflict naming sessionId 01a19e08-ad9f… (steps/bob/problems.jsonl, 58-j7-bob-after-start). compose.ts:3643-3660 runs recoverInterruptedSessions only at start and skips it when sync is paused. A later restart logged 'interrupted sessions ended at start'. Screenshots: steps/bob/43, 49, 51; steps/ada/40, 45.
findings.expected: When a run fails because the store is unreachable, the daemon retries closing the row once the connection is back, or a periodic sweep ends sessions this install no longer runs. Stop all clears this install's dead sessions. The words say the connection was lost.
findings.fix_hint: Queue the session end and claim release in memory and flush them on reconnect. Run recovery for this install's dead rows periodically and on Stop all, not only at compose. Word it 'the connection to the shared state was lost'.

findings.title: No offline mode on the PC: an error banner, an empty Home and lost writes
findings.requirement: ADR 0024 'Paired mode, PC cannot reach Postgres', phase 2 gate, F
findings.what_a_person_meets: With the shared database unreachable, Bob's app says 'Not connected. connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:48778'. Home shows no projects, only 'New project'. A note he sends answers 500 and is lost. The log gains a warning every 500 ms.
findings.evidence: steps/bob/39-bob-home-offline.png. POST /projects/:id/queue answered 500 {code: internal, message: 'connect ECONNREFUSED…'}. No Outbox implementation exists in packages/runtime (grep for flushOutbox / sync/outbox finds it only in apps/ui/src/mobile and services). Bob's daemon.log had 56 ECONNREFUSED lines in about 35 s (remote command poll, approvals poll, scheduler, presence).
findings.expected: As ADR 0024 says: read-only on the last brief with words like 'Working offline: the shared project is not reachable', writes queued and flushed on reconnect, and the log rate-limited.
findings.fix_hint: Implement the runtime outbox (SQLite) behind the store for messages, notes, answers and receipts. Cache the last project list and brief. Back the pollers off while the store is unreachable.

findings.title: No realtime between the two desktops and no polling fallback
findings.what_a_person_meets: Ada adds a task (which sends Bob 'Ada: Added …'). Bob's open Inbox shows nothing for 150 s, and the header badge does not change. The line appears only after he reloads the page.
findings.evidence: j3rt2: 'bob's open Inbox showed it after NOT within 150 s'. In that time the page made only its initial requests (one GET /inbox and the /events stream). server.ts:2511-2585: the daemon's /events relays only in-process rt.events; nothing watches the shared store for other installs' writes. The state service's /health reported realtime.subscribers 0 for the whole walk. Screenshots: steps/bob/22-bob-inbox-realtime-check.png, 23-…-150s.png, 24-bob-inbox-after-reload.png.
findings.expected: Another person's message, card or task change appears within seconds: from LISTEN/NOTIFY or the state service's change feed, else by polling.
findings.fix_hint: Give the daemon a ChangePoller (or the state-api /events client) that turns store changes for this human into inbox.changed and project.changed SSE frames. Add a UI poll of /inbox every 30 s as the fallback.

findings.title: A person cannot send a message or question to the other person or their agent
findings.what_a_person_meets: Bob wants to tell Ada 'I'm taking the FAQ'. The app has no compose box, no Inbox reply, and no chat command for it. Agents' questions (ask_person) go only to their own person, so Ada can never answer a question from Bob's agent.
findings.evidence: server.ts has app.post('/messages/:id/read') but no POST /messages. The chat's 30 command tools (autonomy_set … tasks_list, steps/ada/20-ada-chat-tools) include no message tool. The loop files requests with human_id=deps.humanId (loop/memory.ts:633, repo-create.ts:338, merge.ts:565). Only automated agent messages appeared in the message table.
findings.expected: 'Message Ada' on the project page and in the Inbox, typed (info, question, request, requires-ack), delivered to her Inbox with receipts. A chat intent can do the same.
findings.fix_hint: Add POST /messages (from this human's principal agent to a member human or agent, project-scoped), a compose UI and a message.send command.

findings.title: The other person can read your private chat
findings.what_a_person_meets: Bob opens /sessions/<Ada's conversation id> in his app. He sees Ada's chat with her agent, her lines labelled 'You: share this project with Bob…'.
findings.evidence: Chat lines are stored as chat.human / chat.reply events of a 'conversation' session row (projectId null) in the shared Postgres (session 01a19df2-af73…). server.ts:1453-1455 and 1474: GET /sessions/:id and /sessions/:id/events have no ownership check. Bob's daemon answered 200 with the events (steps/bob/30-bob-views-adas-chat.txt). The state service refuses the same for devices: 'a device sees only sessions of its own human's agents' (state-service.md route table). Bob's daemon also served Ada's work session logs (steps/bob/14).
findings.expected: Chat stays on the person's PC (like private memory) or is readable only by its owner's install. Session logs of another person's agent are limited to what the project shares.
findings.fix_hint: Apply ownsSession (ownership.ts) to /sessions/:id* for conversation rows at least. Consider moving the chat transcript to the private index (ADR 0083).

findings.title: The other person can lower your project's budget silently
findings.requirement: S.10, F (change sentences), design: Changes lists every change
findings.what_a_person_meets: Bob opens Settings → Budget per session → Team site → Change and sets CHF 1. Ada's Settings now shows CHF 1.00. She got no Inbox line, and her Changes page does not list it, so she cannot tell who did it or undo it.
findings.evidence: After Bob's Yes, project.settings gained session_cap_chf_micro 1000000. No message rows were created after 20:50. Ada's Changes page (steps/ada/39-ada-changes-page.txt) has no line from Bob. Screenshots: steps/bob/37-bob-budget-preview.png, steps/ada/38-ada-settings-after-bob-budget.png. Cause: executor.ts:664-672 (see C-05).
findings.expected: Project budget and autonomy belong to the project's owner, or change only with the owner's yes. Every member sees each change with who made it, in Changes and the Inbox.
findings.fix_hint: Mark project money and autonomy keys owner-only for non-owner members, or file the change as a card to the owner. Show other people's change_log rows on Changes, named.

findings.title: 'Create the repository' on a shared project links the presser's private repo; the other person's next session fails with a raw 404
findings.what_a_person_meets: Both people get 'Code work is planned for Team site, which has no repository. Create the repository?'. Bob presses it, and the project is linked to bob/team-site, private, in Bob's account. Ada's card still says the project has no repository. Her press answers 'Done' and does nothing. Her next session fails both tasks with 'Failed: GET /repos/bob/team-site -> 404: Not Found'.
findings.evidence: Bob's daemon.log: 'repository created and linked {repo: bob/team-site}'. project.repos stayed ["bob/team-site"] after Ada's press, with no log line on Ada's side. With Ada's token the fake host answered 'Not Found' for bob/team-site. Ada's Overview: 'Failed: GET /repos/bob/team-site -> 404: Not Found' (steps/ada/56, 57, 60).
findings.expected: For a shared project the repository is created where all members can reach it (an org, or with collaborators added), the card is withdrawn for everyone once one person answers, and a member who cannot reach the repository is told in words what to ask for.
findings.fix_hint: On repo creation, withdraw the other members' cards and add the other members' GitHub logins as collaborators (or ask which owner/org). Before cloning, check access and file 'You don't have access to bob/team-site; ask Bob to add you' instead of failing tasks.

findings.title: On a shared repository project the joiner sees no pull requests, and the owner sees everyone's without names
findings.requirement: F.5, design §3.4 (Waiting for you to merge)
findings.what_a_person_meets: After both agents opened pull requests, Ada's 'Waiting for you to merge' lists all 10, including Bob's #10 and #11, with no name of whose they are. Bob's page shows 'not your project / Retry' instead of any list, so it is unclear who should merge. Both installs' commits are authored 'Alice (Forerunner)'.
findings.evidence: steps/ada/54-ada-j7-overview-prs.txt lists PRs #2-#7 and #9-#12. steps/bob/63-bob-j7-overview-prs.txt shows 'not your project / Retry'. git log on fr/status: commits from both installs authored 'Alice (Forerunner)'. On the fake host, PR #10's user is 'bob'.
findings.expected: Each person sees the pull requests on the shared project, each named by whose agent made it, with one agreed merger: the owner's 2026-11-02 decision (one-click Merge) needs a rule for who merges on a shared project.
findings.fix_hint: Use the same ownership rule for the PR list as for the project list (C-04). Add 'by Ada's agent / by Bob's agent' to each row. Put the person's name in the commit author.

findings.title: Both people's agents are called 'Alice', so nothing says whose agent did what
findings.what_a_person_meets: Bob's Peers shows 'Alice'. His Inbox shows every line from 'Alice', his own agent's and Ada's alike. The chip says 'Alice is working on…' for either agent. Memory shows 'Alice' and 'Alice (peer)'. Bob's refused start says 'Alice is already working…' about his own agent.
findings.evidence: agent table: two principals named 'Alice' (owners Ada and Bob). Screenshots: steps/bob/10-bob-inbox-after-share.png, 11-bob-overview-now.png, steps/bob/33-bob-memory-peer-tab.png.
findings.expected: A peer's agent is shown with its person ('Ada's Alice'), or a joining install picks a different default name.
findings.fix_hint: In shared views, render 'agentName (ownerName)' for agents of other humans. Default a joiner's agent name to something other than an existing principal's name on the store.

findings.title: Peers panel: claims 'expire just now' 30 minutes early, and tasks show as raw ids
findings.what_a_person_meets: Bob's Peers says '… · expires just now' for a claim that expires in 30 minutes. 'Files in flight' reads '01a19dfa-40a5-77e4-…: index.html', and 'Last handoff … Next: 01a19dfd-01ef-…, 01a19dfd-21b4-…'.
findings.evidence: time.ts:44 (Math.max(0, now - t)) turns any future time into 'just now'. PeersSection.tsx renders relativeTime(c.expiresAt), the taskId keys of inFlightFiles and lastHandoff.next as given. The DB claim_expires was 21:07 at 20:37. Screenshots: steps/bob/11-bob-overview-now.txt, 20-bob-overview-both-running.txt, 61-j7b-bob-overview.txt.
findings.expected: 'expires in 30 min', and task titles instead of ids.
findings.fix_hint: Add a future branch to relativeTime ('in N min'). Map task ids to titles in the peer feed view (server side).

findings.title: The schema sync gate works, but its words are jargon and the start dialog first promises a run
findings.requirement: Spec M (compatible version before sync), design writing rules
findings.what_a_person_meets: Inbox: 'Sync with the shared state is paused: this install is at schema 5, the peer at 6: update this install before sync resumes'. The start dialog says 'This session runs "Add alt text…"', then on Start shows the raw 'sync paused: this install is at schema 5, the peer at 6…'. The Peers section silently disappears (503).
findings.evidence: Bob's daemon.log: 'sync paused {source: peer_feed, local 5, peer 6}', then 'sync resumed' after the version row was removed, with the card withdrawn. POST /sessions answered 503 (steps/bob/problems.jsonl). Screenshots: steps/bob/45-bob-inbox-gate.png, 48-bob-palette-started.png. The start-check route does not consult the gate.
findings.expected: 'Ada's Forerunner is newer than yours. Update this app (Updates → Check for updates) to keep working on shared projects.' The start dialog says this before Start is pressed.
findings.fix_hint: Word the card in terms of the other person and the Updates screen. Add the gate state to /projects/:id/start-check and the project status sentence.

findings.title: Receipts and resurfacing happen between agents only; the people never see them
findings.what_a_person_meets: Bob's agent's handoff to Ada's agent goes unread for a while. Bob learns this only as a Details line in his session ('1 message this agent sent is not acknowledged yet.'). Ada's Inbox never shows Bob's agent's handoffs or its overlap 'Heads-up'.
findings.evidence: message rows: handoff Bob's agent → Ada's agent with delivered/read/acted set after Ada's session. Bob's next session logged inbox.unacknowledged {count 1}. The line is visible only under Details (steps/bob/29-bob-session-details2.txt). server.ts:1661-1664: the Inbox lists messages addressed to the human only.
findings.expected: A person sees their peer's handoff on the shared project ('Bob's agent: did 2 tasks …') and can see whether their own agent's note to the peer was read.
findings.fix_hint: Show peer-agent messages on shared projects in Updates. Add a person-level line for unacknowledged handoffs.

findings.title: Overlap warning is sent for a task the agent then does not do
findings.what_a_person_meets: Bob's agent sends Ada's agent: 'Heads-up: I am starting "Add a retry helper to src/app.js" (01a19e0f-eefd-…), which touches src/app.js…'. A second later it sends: 'I planned to work on "Add a retry helper…" but you hold the claim; I moved on.'
findings.evidence: Message rows at 21:00:29 (a warning, then an info). Events: peer.overlap {kind: files} and task.skipped {reason: held_by} for the same plannedTaskId. The overlap check runs before the claim attempt.
findings.expected: Claim first. Warn only about a task this agent actually holds, without the raw id in the text.
findings.fix_hint: In the runner, move detectOverlap's files message after a successful claim, or drop it when the claim fails.

findings.title: The change sentence to the other person shows a raw id and offers an Undo they cannot use
findings.what_a_person_meets: Bob's Inbox: 'Ada: Set who the project is shared with for Team site from unset to ["01a19df1-4653-…"]. Undo in Changes', signed by 'Alice'. Bob's Changes has no such entry to undo.
findings.evidence: steps/bob/10-bob-inbox-after-share.png. executor.ts:664-672 sends the sentence as written for the actor.
findings.expected: 'Ada shared Team site with you.' with no Undo for someone who did not make the change.
findings.fix_hint: Write a separate sentence for other members, render names for human ids, and leave out the Undo pointer.

findings.title: Task rows and Last result do not say whose agent did the work
findings.what_a_person_meets: On a shared project the Tasks tab shows 'Who does it: coder' for every task. Last result shows whichever session ended last ('Did 2 tasks …') without saying it was Bob's agent. New task offers no way to give a task to the other person's agent.
findings.evidence: steps/bob/15-bob-tasks-tab.txt, steps/ada/31-ada-overview-after-bob-handoff.txt. The New task 'Who does it' options are the specialists and 'Me' only (newtask labels).
findings.expected: Rows and Last result name the person whose agent holds or did the task. Optionally 'Ada's agent' / 'Bob's agent' appear as choices.
findings.fix_hint: Add the claimant's or owner's human name to the TaskView and the session summary view for other humans' agents.

findings.title: The person docs promise sharing that does not exist as described
findings.what_a_person_meets: The user guide says 'Peers appear only when another agent works on the project' and that the agent 'claims tasks so it never collides with your collaborator's agent'. But the owner never sees Peers (C-05), and nothing explains how to get a collaborator at all.

Root causes that cover most findings, for the fixers:
1. Identity: binding the 'only' human lets a new install become the first person (C-01).
2. Two membership models that disagree: settings.members (agent ids, owner only), used by peers and handoffs, versus settings.shared_with (human ids), used by change sentences and ownsProject. Plus routes that apply neither (/projects, /tasks, /sessions, /chat) (C-03, C-04, C-05, C-13, C-15).
3. Desktops are direct Postgres clients with no change feed and no outbox, so there is no realtime and no offline mode, and a dropped connection strands session rows (C-08, C-09, C-10).
4. Project views read 'any session or any file on the project' without filtering by install (C-06, C-07, C-22).

findings.summary:
I reviewed the collaboration code at HEAD df361fc and ran the existing collaboration tests against a private Postgres 16 on 127.0.0.1:55493, which I have since stopped and deleted. All of them pass:
- Integration: 66 of 66 (state-api.integration 3, state postgres 60, migrations 1, cloud-runner 2), plus 2 of 2 for phase2-gate and memory postgres.
- Unit: 330 of 330 in 31 collaboration files.
- E2E: scenarios 04-collision, 08-handover and 09-phone, 4 of 4.

The tests miss real collaboration bugs because their worlds seed `settings.members` with both agents (scenario-world.ts:889-894, peers.test.ts:70) and drive one process or the store directly. Thirteen findings, all measured with scratch probes on the shared Postgres unless the finding says code reading only:
- **Wrong person stops a session:** Stop now on the other person's live session ends its row as "Stopped by you." and frees its claims while it keeps running (P9).
- **Peers only one way:** the agent of the person who created a project never treats the collaborator's agent as a peer: no handoff, no peer feed, no overlap warnings (P1).
- **Claims:** a claim that lapsed while its run went on is taken by the peer, and both agents run the task (P2). A task in review whose holder's PC never returns stays claimed and in review forever, and a ghost session shows the peer "online" forever (P3, P5).
- **Unmerged PRs:** accepted PRs that wait for Merge (the owner's new default) are invisible to the peer feed (P4).
- **Privacy and control:** the other person's phone lists, reads and changes unshared projects (P8). A message starting with "stop" from the other person ends my session as "Stopped after the task, as asked." (P6 plus P8).
- **Realtime:** the poller loses rows written by a PC whose clock is behind (P7).
- **Smaller:** false words on shared projects, Undo of a cancel made across PCs, the sync gate pausing mid-session, the PC's offline outbox, and push wording.

findings.title: Stop now / Stop after this task on the other person's live session marks it stopped and frees its claims while it keeps running
findings.requirement: F.4 claim-before-work; design §4.9/§4.10 (Stop now, dead-session end); ADR 0041 item 4 (the daemon acts as its own human only)
findings.what_a_person_meets: Ada's project card says Bobby is working on "Header" and links to his session. She opens it and presses Stop now. Bob's session row now reads "Stopped by you. \"Header\" is ready again." Bob never stopped, and the session did not stop either: Bob's PC drops that run, goes on with the next task and then takes "Header" again. Bob's session row stays "stopped" whatever his runner does after.
findings.evidence: server.ts:1545-1566: POST /sessions/:id/stop checks `rt.kill.activeCount({sessionId})`, which is always 0 in Ada's process for a session on Bob's PC, so it calls `endDeadSession`. That releases every claim of Bob's agent in the project (recovery.ts:96-110) and sets the row to stopped. The pause route at :1572ff has the same else-branch. Neither route checks ownership: /sessions at :1357-1377 and /sessions/:id at :1453 do not, and `ownsSession` is used only at :2472. `workingOn` (project-status.ts:318-345) picks any agent's running session for the card, and its link is at :177. Probe P9 (/tmp/frbench/collab/review/probe/probe-p9.out): adaDaemonSeesLiveRun false; afterAdaStop {session:stopped, summary:'Stopped by you. "Header" is ready again.', task:ready, claimedBy:null}; bobRunStillRegistered true; bobRunnerAfter {status:completed, inReview:2, startedTasks:[Header,Footer,Header]}; bobSessionRowFinal status stopped.
findings.expected: A session another install runs is never ended as dead from this install. Its page either has no Stop buttons for another person, or stops it through that install: a remote command with an owner check, which the other PC's watcher acts on. The words say whose session it is.
findings.fix_hint: In the stop and pause routes, treat a row as dead only when it is this install's: `s.device_id === rt.remote.device?.id` and its agent is this human's, as `recoverInterruptedSessions` already filters (recovery.ts:181-186). For other rows, refuse with NOT_YOURS or enqueue a remote command. Filter /sessions, /sessions/:id and `workingOn` links with `ownsSession`, or mark them read-only in the view.

findings.title: The agent of the person who created a project never treats the collaborator's agent as a peer (no handoff, no feed, no overlap warning)
findings.requirement: F.6 peer awareness, F.7 handoff note at every session end
findings.what_a_person_meets: Ada creates a project in the app and shares it with Bob. Bob's agent gets Ada's... no: it is the other way round. Ada's agent gets Bob's handoffs. Bob's agent gets nothing from Ada's sessions: no handoff, no 'you hold the claim' notes, no file overlap warnings. Ada's Overview never shows Bob in Peers.
findings.evidence: create-project.ts:64 writes `settings: { members: [deps.agent.id] }`. `defaultPeers` (runner.ts:3143-3153) returns only `members` when the list is non-empty. No setting or route adds a member agent: the only sharing setting is `shared_with`, which holds human ids (commands/settings.ts:238-246), and `ownsProject` accepts it (commands/ownership.ts:28). Probe P1 (/tmp/frbench/collab/review/probe/probe-runtime.out): bobOwnsProject true; peersOf(Alice) []; peersOf(Bobby) [Alice]; after one session each: handoffsInBobbyInbox [], handoffsInAliceInbox [{from:Bobby, requiresAck:true}]; aliceFeedPeers []. The tests seed both agents as members (tests/e2e/src/scenario-world.ts:889-894, tests/e2e/src/world.ts:453, packages/runtime/test/peers.test.ts:70), so none of them meets this.
findings.expected: Sharing a project makes each person's principal agent a peer of the other in both directions.
findings.fix_hint: Have `defaultPeers` include the principal agents of the `shared_with` humans and of `author_human`, or add the collaborator's agent to `members` when the project is shared. Add a test that creates the project through `createProjectRecord` and shares it via `shared_with`.

findings.title: A claim that lapsed during a run is taken by the peer while the holder keeps working; both run the task and one person's work replaces the other's
findings.requirement: F.4 claim-before-work with expiry; F.5 code only via branches and PRs
findings.what_a_person_meets: Ada's laptop sleeps for 31 minutes in the middle of a task. Bob's next session takes the task. When the laptop wakes, Ada's run carries on, so both agents build the same task. Ada's agent then moves the task Bob holds to review. Bob's log says the task "was moved to in_review while it ran; its run was stopped". The PR ends up with whichever push came last.
findings.evidence: The renewal error is swallowed: `void store.task.renewClaim(...).catch(() => undefined)` (runner.ts:1395). The task watch checks only `row.status !== "in_progress"` (runner.ts:2637) and never `claimed_by`. The claim SQL accepts a lapsed claim on an in_progress task (task.ts:125-126), and `expireClaims` runs at every session start (runner.ts:872). After the run, the runner reads the task and acts on it whoever now holds it (runner.ts:1513-1546). Both PCs use the same branch name per task (pr-executor.ts:168-171) and push with --force-with-lease (git.ts:526; pr-executor.ts:258, 398). Probe P2: bothRunningSameTask [alice, bob]; rowWhileBothRun {in_progress, claimedBy Bobby}; aliceRenewAfterTakeover claim_conflict; aliceRunStillGoingAfterWatchTicks true; taskAfter {in_review, pr: alice's, owner Alice}; bobLogLine '"Rate limiter" was moved to in_review while it ran; its run was stopped and the session goes on'.
findings.expected: An agent that lost its claim stops that task's run at once and never moves or pushes the task. Only the current holder writes.
findings.fix_hint: When renewClaim fails with claim_conflict, abort the task's controller (`kill.stopTask`). Have the watch also stop the run when `claimed_by !== agent.id`. Before the post-run transitions and before the push, check `claimed_by === agent.id`, and record 'lost the claim' in words. Consider a version-checked renewal.

findings.title: The other person's phone/web, and the desktop, list, read and change projects that were never shared with them
findings.requirement: S.10 privacy between collaborators; `shared_with` setting ('Human ids that see the project's data')
findings.what_a_person_meets: Bob's phone lists Ada's private side project, shows its task titles, and lets him cancel one of its tasks or add a note to it. Ada's desktop lists Bob's projects too. Yet her Docs, queue and Read aloud for those projects answer 'not your project'.
findings.evidence: services/state-api/src/routes/projects.ts:51-62 (GET /projects lists every active project), :88-105 (tasks), :116-131 (POST /tasks/:id/transition with no project check), :182-205 (queue). `ownsProject` appears nowhere in services/state-api/src. On the daemon, server.ts:859-862 (/projects), :1016-1022 (tasks) and :1210-1231 (transition) have no ownership check, while docs-routes.ts:182, queue-routes.ts:50/77 and server.ts:2456 refuse another human's project. Probe P8 (/tmp/frbench/collab/review/probe/probe-stateapi.out): bobPhoneProjects ['Ada private','Demo']; bobPhoneSeesTasks ["Ada's secret task"]; bobPhoneCancelsAdasTask {http:200, status:cancelled, authorHuman:Bob}; bobPhoneQueuesNote 201. ADR 0041:110-111 keeps project views project-wide, which assumes every project on the store is shared.
findings.expected: One rule, `ownsProject`, for every project, task, decision, queue and upload route on both the daemon and the state service. A project not shared with a person is invisible to them and cannot be changed by them.
findings.fix_hint: Add `ownsProject` filtering to the state-api project, task, decision, queue, upload and realtime (`task`, `project`, `decision`) paths for device principals, and to the daemon's /projects, /projects/:id/tasks and /tasks/:id/* routes. Amend ADR 0041 to match. Tests: another human's unshared project returns 404/403 on every route.

findings.title: A message from the other person (or their agent) that starts with "stop", "pause" or "halt" ends my session as "Stopped after the task, as asked."
findings.requirement: F.1 typed messages; R.4 / ADR 0041 8b (remote control is owner-filtered); design §4.9 (who stopped it is said)
findings.what_a_person_meets: Bob sends Ada's agent a note from his phone: "Stop worrying about the footer, I have it." Ada's running session ends after its current task. Her result reads "Stopped after the task, as asked.", but she asked nothing.
findings.evidence: runner.ts:136 `STOP_WORD_RE = /^\s*(stop|halt|pause)\b/i`. runner.ts:3015 applies it to every unread non-handoff message in the agent's inbox, whoever sent it, and the between-tasks check at runner.ts:1296-1301 ends the session with stopped_by_message. state-api inbox.ts:80-110 `sendMessageAs` checks only that the sender is the device's own human's agent; `toAgentId` can be anyone's (written at :94). Wording: result.ts:92-94, stop-words.ts:60-61. Probe P6: aliceSession {status:stopped, stopReason:stopped_by_message, completed:1, skipped:1} after Bobby's message. Probe P8: bobPhoneMessagesAdasAgent 201 with body 'Stop for now please'.
findings.expected: Only the agent's own human, through the pause port's own message (session-ports.ts PAUSE_BODY_RE), or a remote command that passed the owner filter, can stop or pause a session. A peer's note is just a message.
findings.fix_hint: Act on a stop word only when the message is from the agent itself (the pause port's message) or authored by `agent.owner_human_id`. Better still, match the pause-port body format only. Name the stopper in the words.

findings.title: A task in review whose holder's PC never comes back stays claimed and 'being reviewed' forever; a ghost session shows the peer 'online' forever
findings.requirement: F.4 'Claims expire'; state-service.md offline story ('Its claims lapse after 30 minutes, so nothing on the other PC waits for it')
findings.what_a_person_meets: Bob's PC dies during a critic review, or Bob stops using Forerunner. On Ada's side the task reads 'being reviewed' and claimed by Bobby for good. Her sessions never take it, the milestone never closes, and her Peers section shows Bobby with a green 'online' badge a week later.
findings.evidence: KEEPS_CLAIM includes in_review (task.ts:18). renewClaim only renews claimed and in_progress tasks (task.ts:165-167), so it cannot renew during a review. expireClaims only expires claimed and in_progress tasks (task.ts:204). The claim SQL refuses in_review (task.ts:126). Recovery only handles this install's own agents and device (recovery.ts:177-186; the module comment says 'a row another device ran is that device's'). `online` is true for any session row in running or paused status, with no heartbeat (peers.ts:141); the badge is rendered at PeersSection.tsx:44-48. Probe P3: renewInReview claim_conflict; after48h {expired:0, status:in_review, claimedBy:Bobby, aliceClaim:not_claimable}; aliceFeedOfBobby {claims:0, openPrs:0}. Probe P5: bobbyOnlineAWeekLater true.
findings.expected: An in-review claim lapses like the others when nobody renews it, or the reviewing session renews it. A peer's session that stopped heartbeating reads 'offline', and its review goes back to ready under the rules of reviewBackToReady.
findings.fix_hint: Renew claims through the review as well, or give in_review its own expiry in expireClaims that routes through `reviewBackToReady`. Derive `online` from the device heartbeat (`device.last_seen`, remote/presence.ts) or the session's last event time, not the status alone.

findings.title: Accepted pull requests waiting for Merge (the owner's new default) are invisible to the peer feed, so the peer edits the same files unwarned
findings.requirement: F.6 overlap detection on files and tasks; owner decision 2026-11-02 ('the person presses Merge' by default)
findings.what_a_person_meets: Bob's agent finishes 'Rate limiter'. The critic accepts it and the PR waits for Bob to press Merge. Ada's agent then starts work on src/rate-limit.ts with no heads-up, and the second PR conflicts.
findings.evidence: peers.ts:129-136 counts openPullRequests only for tasks in `in_review`. The handoff's `in_flight_files` lists only tasks still in review at session end (runner.ts:2242-2245). A done task's claim is cleared (task.ts:255-258). Scenario 04 itself ends with tasks done and 2 open PRs (04-collision.scenario.test.ts:178-191). Probe P4: feedForUnmergedDonePR {openPrs:0, claims:0, filesInFlight:[]}.
findings.expected: A done task whose PR is still open counts as in flight for peers: it shows under open PRs, and its changed files take part in the file overlap check until the PR is merged.
findings.fix_hint: In buildPeerFeed, include tasks that are done with `pr_url` set and an unmerged PR (from the host, or a merged flag), with their files from the `task.files` events of the session that did them. Carry them in the handoff's `in_flight_files` until they are merged.

findings.title: Realtime poller never announces rows written by a PC whose clock is behind another writer's (no SSE event, no push)
findings.requirement: F.3 realtime push with polling fallback
findings.what_a_person_meets: Ada's PC clock runs 90 s fast. Bob's agent sends Ada's agent a question. No change event and no phone notification ever come for it. It shows only when something re-reads the inbox.
findings.evidence: realtime.ts:406 `WHERE "${w.column}" >= ?` with the mark advanced to the newest row timestamp (:414). Those timestamps come from each writer's own clock, through `this.clock.nowIso()` in the repositories (for example task.ts:131). Probe P7 (two stores on one Postgres schema, one clock 90 s ahead): announced {m1:true, m2:false, m1UpdatedAt 09:01:30, m2UpdatedAt 09:00:10}. A transaction that commits after a later row was polled is missed the same way.
findings.expected: Every committed row is announced once, whatever the writers' clocks say.
findings.fix_hint: Poll on a server-side sequence or commit time: a `bigserial` change sequence, `xmin`, or the database's `now()` set by default or trigger. Or keep an overlap window (mark minus N seconds), since (table, id, version) dedupe already exists.

findings.title: Cancel from one PC of a task the other PC is running: its work is taken out of the folder on the other PC, and Undo on the cancelling PC silently cannot bring it back
findings.requirement: design §3.5 (every action has one Undo), phase C live walk 2 C1 (a cancel's work is set aside, Undo brings it back)
findings.what_a_person_meets: Ada cancels a task Bob's agent is running. Her line says only "Cancelled X.", yet Bob's PC removes the run's changes from its folder. Ada presses Undo: the task is reopened, but the work stays set aside on Bob's PC and nothing says so.
findings.evidence: Code reading only, not probed. The cancel's `stopped` comes from the local `kill.stopTask` (commands/task.ts:330-346; compose.ts:2978), which is false for another PC's run, so `work` is undefined. Bob's runner sets the files aside because its watch's `kill.stopTask` makes `stoppedByMove` true (runner.ts:842-858; watch at :2637-2638). Undo calls `bringBackWork` through this PC's executor (compose.ts:2981-2984; commands/task.ts:440-452). That looks in Ada's worktree, finds nothing, returns 'missing', and no sentence is said.
findings.expected: The cancel's words and its Undo describe what really happened on the PC that ran the task, or that PC brings the work back on Undo.
findings.fix_hint: Set aside only when this install's own route stopped the run, or record the set-aside ref and its device on the task. Have the Undo enqueue a 'bring back' for that device, or say 'its changes are kept on Bob's computer'.

findings.title: Words that are untrue on a two-person project
findings.requirement: design §5 (true words); owner's complaint class 'says something untrue'
findings.what_a_person_meets: Ada sees Bob's sign-off listed as 'Accepted by you at sign-off', and the task's reason reads 'you accepted the work at sign-off'. Her 'Waiting for you to merge' lists Bob's PRs. Her Overview 'Last result' is whichever person's session ended last, for example Bob's 'Stopped by you.'.
findings.evidence: The reason is stored on the shared row: findings.ts:322 `ACCEPTED_AT_SIGNOFF = "you accepted the work at sign-off"`. pull-requests.ts:68-73 maps it to 'you', and SummaryTab.tsx:226 labels it 'Accepted by you at sign-off'. pull-requests.ts:96-110 lists every done task's PR, while the doc comment at :78 says 'a PR of someone else's is not listed'. The project has a single `summary_cache.last_session` written by every agent's session end (runner.ts:2393-2410), shown by views.ts:277-283, and its summary carries stopWords such as 'Stopped by you.' (result.ts:86-87). Probe P2 log: '"Rate limiter" was moved to in_review while it ran'.
findings.expected: Who did it is named: 'Bob accepted it at sign-off', 'Bob's session'. Lists of PRs to merge say whose they are.
findings.fix_hint: Store who signed off, as `author_human` or a name, rather than 'you'. Render 'you' only when it is the viewer. Keep a last session per agent or per human in summary_cache, or show the agent's name with it.

findings.title: A sync pause mid-session fails the session, and session end still writes to the shared store
findings.requirement: spec M (compatible version before sync resumes); updates.md 'The wired gate'
findings.what_a_person_meets: Bob updates his install and the shared schema moves ahead. Ada's running session shows 'Failed' at its next task. The session-end writes, handoffs and the project summary cache, still go to the shared store that the gate says not to touch.
findings.evidence: Code reading only, not probed. buildPeerFeed calls `schemaSync.assertCanSync` before every task (peers.ts:110-113, runner.ts:1315). The outer catch makes 'unavailable' a failed session (runner.ts:1968-1980). Session end then sends the handoffs (runner.ts:2421-2431) and patches summary_cache (runner.ts:2393-2410). The gate's own card says 'Until then no session starts and no approval, mirror run or peer feed is read' (update/sync.ts:212).
findings.expected: The session stops at the boundary with a 'sync paused' stop reason in words, and nothing is written to the shared store while paused.
findings.fix_hint: Catch 'unavailable' from the per-task feed as a stop reason, for example `sync_paused` with its own words. Skip shared writes at session end while `schemaSync.paused`.

findings.title: The PC's offline story (read-only on the last brief, outbox for messages, receipts and answers) is documented but not implemented in the runtime
findings.requirement: R.3 offline queue; phase 2 gate ('either install can be offline for 48 simulated hours')
findings.what_a_person_meets: When a PC loses the shared Postgres, nothing queues. Its sessions fail on the first store call, and no outbound message, receipt or answer is kept for later.
findings.evidence: state-service.md, 'Offline story': 'Paired mode, Postgres unreachable: the PC stays read-only on its last state brief ... queues ... in an Outbox'. `flushOutbox`, `MemoryOutbox` and `/sync/outbox` appear only in services/state-api and apps/ui/src/mobile, never in packages/runtime (grep). The 48-hour gate test drives the store directly and queues on 'Bob's phone' (state-api.integration.test.ts:237-300), not on a PC runtime.
findings.expected: Either the runtime implements the PC side, or the doc and the gate evidence say that only the phone queues and that a PC without the store stops.
findings.fix_hint: Correct state-service.md and gates.md now. If the PC side is wanted, wrap the daemon's shared writes for messages, receipts and answers in an Outbox flushed through `/sync/outbox`.

findings.title: Phone push says 'New message: Open the inbox to read it.' for agent-to-agent notes no Inbox shows
findings.what_a_person_meets: Each handoff or overlap note Bob's agent sends Ada's agent buzzes Ada's phone with 'Open the inbox to read it.' Neither her phone's Inbox nor her desktop Inbox lists it. This stays hidden until Firebase is set up.
findings.evidence: fanout.ts:331-357 pushes any unread message to the human's agent from another human's agent. The Inbox routes list only `to_human_id` messages (state-api inbox.ts:236-238; daemon server.ts:1660-1663).
findings.expected: Either no push for messages addressed to the agent, or the Inbox shows the peer agents' notes to the person.
findings.fix_hint: In `fanout.notices`, push only when `row.to_human_id === e.humanId`. Or add a 'From Bob's agent' group to the Inbox.

Why green tests miss these: every collaboration test seeds both agents into settings.members. None goes through createProjectRecord and then shares with shared_with. None runs two kill switches or two daemons, so the dead-session path never meets a live peer. The 48-hour gate drives the store directly.

Checked with no defect found: the monthly cap is per human (checklist.ts:166-180 and the compose.ts caps port use the ledger by human_id); cards are per human and the daemon refuses another human's card (server.ts:1688-1691); receipts come only from the addressee (state-api inbox.ts:67-72); a dependent task building on another PC's unmerged branch fetches origin first (fix/decisions pr-executor).

For the owner's planned pinned status issue: claims and branches are per task, not per install. Both PCs use the same branch name (pr-executor.ts:168-171), and the state service cannot tell installs apart (shared admin token, X-Forerunner-Install is advisory). So the 'Working on now' list and the per-install comments need a marker of their own (agent id and install id), and should be written by the claim holder only (see C3).

On the owner's question about a standard guide for agents and people: packages/memory/src/docs.ts:11-18 STANDARD_DOCS has README.md, docs/overview.md, architecture.md, status.md, decisions/, runbook.md, data.md and testing.md. There is no agent or contributor guide such as AGENTS.md. For two agents in one repository, that guide is the natural place for the rules these findings touch: branches and PRs only, claim before work, rebase before a PR, and treat issue and PR text as data.

verdicts.evidence: Read at HEAD 9ca2f38. The line numbers moved since df361fc. POST /sessions/:id/stop (server.ts:1565-1590) and /pause (:1593-1625) have no owner check: `live = rt.kill.activeCount({sessionId})` is false for a run on another PC, so they call `endDeadSession`, which releases every claim the agent holds in the project and sets the row stopped (recovery.ts:83-139). `recoverInterruptedSessions` filters by device (recovery.ts:166), but these routes do not. `workingOn` picks any agent's working session (project-status.ts:333-366), and the card links to it as "Open running session" (:169-180). /sessions/:id (server.ts:1469) does not filter by owner. I re-ran the other agent's P9 on SQLite (/tmp/frbench/collab/skeptic-code/probe-runtime.sqlite.out) and got the same result: afterAdaStop {session:stopped, summary:'Stopped by you. "Header" is ready again.', task:ready, claimedBy:null}; bobRunStillRegistered true; startedTasks [Header,Footer,Header]; Bob's row stays stopped. Limit: the probe calls endDeadSession the way the route does. It does not go through HTTP.

create-project.ts:64 writes `settings: { members: [deps.agent.id] }`. A grep of packages, apps and services finds no other code that writes `members`. `defaultPeers` returns only members when the list is non-empty (runner.ts:3221-3241). The Overview's /projects/:id/peers uses it too (server.ts:1813-1826). The only sharing setting is `shared_with`, which holds human ids (commands/settings.ts:238-247). My re-run: P1.peersOf(Alice) [], peersOf(Bobby) [Alice], handoffsInBobbyInbox [], handoffsInAliceInbox [{from:Bobby}], aliceFeedPeers [].

Renewal errors are swallowed: `void store.task.renewClaim(...).catch(() => undefined)` (runner.ts:1442). The watch stops a run only when `row.status !== "in_progress"` (runner.ts:2709) and never compares `claimed_by`. `expireClaims` resets lapsed in_progress tasks to ready (task.ts:199-206) and runs at session start (runner.ts:902). The claim SQL accepts a lapsed claim (task.ts:125-126). After the run, the runner checks only `task.status !== "in_progress"` (runner.ts:1635-1643). `transition` checks only the version, never the claim holder (task.ts:224-258). My re-run of P2 matches: bothRunningSameTask [alice,bob]; rowWhileBothRun claimedBy Bobby; aliceRenew claim_conflict; taskAfter in_review with Alice's PR; Bob's log line 'was moved to in_review while it ran'. One correction: 'the PR ends up with whichever push came last' is overstated. The first finisher's move to in_review makes the other's watch stop its run within taskWatchMs (5 s, runner.ts:595), so usually only one pushes. A runner that started with no open PR pushes without force (pr-executor.ts:209-215, 258), so a late push is refused rather than replacing the other's.

The state service has no `ownsProject` anywhere in services/state-api/src (grep). GET /projects lists every active project (routes/projects.ts:51-62). Tasks (:88-105) and POST /tasks/:id/transition (:116-131) check only that the row exists. On the daemon, /projects (server.ts:861-864), /projects/:id/tasks (:1018-1024) and /tasks/:id/transition (:1212-1233) have no owner check, while docs-routes.ts:195, queue-routes.ts:50/77 and server.ts:2515 refuse another human's project. My re-run of P8 (/tmp/frbench/collab/skeptic-code/probe-stateapi.sqlite.out): bobPhoneProjects ['Ada private','Demo'], bobPhoneSeesTasks ["Ada's secret task"], cancel http 200 by Bob, queue note 201. Citation fix: the rule 'Task, milestone, decision and project views stay project-wide' is in ADR 0009:110-111, not ADR 0041.

The mechanism is real. `STOP_WORD_RE` (runner.ts:136) is applied to every unread non-handoff message whoever sent it (runner.ts:3093-3100), and the between-tasks check ends the session as stopped_by_message (runner.ts:1326-1331). sendMessageAs accepts any `toAgentId` (state-api inbox.ts:79-110). My re-run of P6 gives stopReason stopped_by_message. I lowered it to minor because no shipped surface reaches it. No phone screen sends a message: apps/ui/src/mobile has no sendMessage caller, and `message.send` appears only in the outbox kind list (mobile/outbox.ts:14). The daemon has no POST /messages. The runtime's own peer texts start with 'I planned…' or 'Heads-up:' (peers.ts:302-312), 'Revision requested…' (findings.ts:741) or 'PR comment by…' (githost-watcher.ts:741). Today only a direct API call or a future feature sets it off. It should still be closed before agent-to-agent notes arrive.

KEEPS_CLAIM includes in_review (task.ts:18). renewClaim renews only claimed and in_progress (task.ts:164-166), and expireClaims only claimed and in_progress (task.ts:204). Recovery handles only this install's agents and device (recovery.ts:160-170). `online` is any running or paused row, with no heartbeat (peers.ts:141), and the badge is at PeersSection.tsx:48. The Tasks tab says 'Being reviewed: The critic is checking the work.' (task-words.ts:233-250). My re-run: P3 after48h in_review, claimedBy Bobby, aliceClaim not_claimable; P5 online a week later true. I lowered it to minor. It needs Bob's PC to crash (or its daemon to die) mid-review and never start Forerunner again, because his startup recovery repairs it (recovery.ts:150-170). A person can also clear it with Cancel then Reopen (task-words.ts:25-26). The untrue 'being reviewed' line and the online badge stay true complaints.

openPullRequests counts only `status === "in_review"` (peers.ts:129-136). The handoff's in_flight_files covers only inReview (runner.ts:2304-2306). A done task's claim is cleared (task.ts:255-258). This already applies today, not only after the new default: pull-requests.ts:76-78 says that below level 3 merging is the person's, and the default autonomy is 2 (create-project.ts:52-53). So every accepted task waits as done with an open PR for as long as the person takes to merge, and F.6's file overlap check never sees it. My re-run: P4 {openPrs:0, claims:0, filesInFlight:[]}.

realtime.ts:400-418 polls `WHERE "<column>" >= mark` and moves the mark to the newest row timestamp. The header comment says PC writes are seen only through this poller, with no triggers (realtime.ts:12-18). Repositories stamp updated_at with the writer's clock (task.ts:131). I reproduced it without Postgres: the same poller over one SQLite file shared by two stores, one clock 90 s ahead (/tmp/frbench/collab/skeptic-code/probe-p7-sqlite.ts) gave {m1:true, m2:false}. A commit that lands after a later row was polled is missed the same way, even with correct clocks.

Code reading, as the claim says. A cancel's `work` is set only when the local `stopTask` stopped a run (commands/task.ts:387-401). The compose port is `kill.stopTask(...).stoppedRuns > 0` (compose.ts:3022 at 9ca2f38), which is false for another PC's run. On that PC the watch's `kill.stopTask` aborts the task controller, `stoppedByMove` is true (runner.ts:836-837, 2709-2711), and the cancelled task is set aside (runner.ts:872-876). Undo calls `bringBackWork`, which uses this PC's executor and local repo (compose.ts:3025-3028; pr-executor.ts:312-317). It says nothing unless the result is restored or conflict (commands/task.ts:500-508), so a missing ref is silent.

The sign-off reason is stored on the shared row as `ACCEPTED_AT_SIGNOFF = "you accepted the work at sign-off"` (findings.ts:322, 616). It maps to 'you' (pull-requests.ts:69) and the label 'Accepted by you at sign-off' (SummaryTab.tsx:235). `summary_cache.last_session` is written by any agent's session end (runner.ts:2457-2470) and shown by views.ts:293-300. My P9 re-run shows the cached summary in another agent's words. One correction: the doc comment at pull-requests.ts:78 ('a PR of someone else's is not listed') means PRs with no Forerunner task and no docs branch (the else branch at :103-115), not the collaborator's PRs. Listing Bob's PRs without saying whose is still unclear wording, but the comment was misread.

Code reading. buildPeerFeed calls `schemaSync.assertCanSync("peer_feed")` (peers.ts:110-113), and the runner rebuilds the feed before every task (runner.ts:1345). The outer catch turns any code other than killed, timeout or budget_exceeded into status failed (runner.ts:2019-2034). The session-end writes run after it: the summary_cache patch (runner.ts:2457ff) and the handoffs. The gate's card promises otherwise (update/sync.ts:212).

state-service.md:325-337 says the PC stays read-only and queues in an Outbox. A grep for flushOutbox, MemoryOutbox and /sync/outbox finds only services/state-api, apps/ui/src/api/state-client.ts and apps/ui/src/mobile, never packages/runtime. The 48-hour gate test queues on 'Bob's phone' (state-api.integration.test.ts:237, 282-349). The gates.md:32 evidence says 'B ... flushes its outbox', which reads as the PC.

fanout.ts:331-357 pushes any unread message whose sender's owner is another human, including those with to_agent_id only. messageHuman resolves the agent to its owner (inbox.ts:44-50). The phone and desktop Inbox read `inbox({humanId})`, which filters on to_human_id (message.ts:23-31; state-client.ts:362), so the pushed note is never listed. It is dormant until Firebase is set up (state-service.md known issues).

findings.summary:
The listed tests for F.1-F.7 and S.10 all exist and all pass. With a private Postgres 16 on port 5463: integration 7 files / 73 tests; unit 26 files / 329 tests; UI 2 files / 26 tests; e2e scenarios 04 and 08, 2 tests. But no test runs two real daemons or two UIs on one shared store. Every F.4/F.6/F.7 test builds the membership straight into the store, a state the app never writes: `settings.members` is set in phase2-gate, scenario-world and daemon.test, all on one in-memory SQLite with hand-built runners and, in phase2-gate and daemon.test, one human. CI runs the Postgres tests on both OS, and at HEAD df361fc that step passed. Every local merge this round skipped them (baseline: 6 files and 71 tests skipped; the fixer prompt calls that "expected"). I then ran two real daemons with the stand-in model on one Postgres and drove both UIs. That found problems no test can catch today:
- (1) A Stop pressed on one PC ends the other PC's running session in the shared store. Its claim is released and the same task runs twice. The cause is this round's dead-session path (86c1e27).
- (2) Peer awareness and handoffs only work one way. The person who creates a project never has peers, because the app writes `members:[creator]` and nothing ever adds the collaborator.
- (3) Neither the app nor the docs give a person a way to join a shared store or share a project. The only control is an Advanced setting that takes a JSON array of human ids.
- (4) A second install with no email silently becomes the first person. Once a second person joins, the first person's install refuses to start.
- (5) The daemon applies no ownership check to project lists, tasks, sessions or session-start. Bob read Ada's unshared project and her session handoff (including her spend), added tasks to it and ran sessions on it.
- (6) A shared project without a repository has no shared code. Each PC works in its own folder, and both screens say "Done: all 6 tasks".
- (7) One desktop does not see the other's changes until a reload.
- (8) Both agents are named "Alice".
I propose a two-daemon real-daemon test, a two-person bench journey (with what scripts/bench needs) and a phase F live journey.

findings.title: Stop on one PC ends the other PC's running session and frees its task for duplicate work
findings.requirement: F.4 (claim-before-work), E.5, S.10; this round's session-engine change 86c1e27 (2026-11-01)
findings.what_a_person_meets: Bob opens the session Ada's PC is running (his app lists it) and presses Stop. Ada's session reads "Stopped by you" although she pressed nothing, her task goes back to ready, and Bob's agent then takes the same task while Ada's PC is still finishing it. Same task done twice, each copy in a different folder.
findings.evidence: packages/runtime/src/daemon/server.ts:1545-1558: when the session is not live in this process (`rt.kill.activeCount`), the route calls `endDeadSession` with no owner or device check. git blame: 86c1e27, this round. /sessions/:id/pause at server.ts:1573 does the same for a session "nothing in this process runs". Bench (two daemons, one Postgres, stand-in model, FORERUNNER_BENCH_DELAY_MS=3000 on Ada), /tmp/frbench/collab/tests/probe/p8.out: Bob POST /sessions/<Ada's running session>/stop -> 200, status stopped, "Stopped by you. \"Ada slow task 1: write notes/slow-1.md\" is ready again." Tasks right after: all 3 ready. Bob's next session: peers.feed shows Alice online:false, claims 0, then task.started and task.finished on Ada slow task 1. Ada's events: session.ended(stopped), then task.finished for the same task, then a second session.ended. Startup recovery is scoped to this install's agents and device (packages/runtime/src/session/recovery.ts:49-55), but the stop and pause routes are not. No test composes two runtimes on one store (real-daemon.test.ts uses one sqlite per case).
findings.expected: Two-daemon real-daemon test (see T-14). Install A runs a session held mid-task. Through B's daemon: POST /sessions/:id/stop, POST /sessions/:id/pause and POST /kill. Assert A's session row stays running, A's claim is kept, and A's run finishes once. B's answer refuses with words naming whose computer runs it. B's next session skips A's task (held_by). Every task has exactly one coder run. A UI case: B's session page for A's session shows no Stop button, or one that explains.
findings.fix_hint: Record which install or device runs a session (the session row has device context for recovery). Treat a row as dead only when this install ran it, and refuse or forward the stop otherwise. Add the case to real-daemon.test.ts per validation rule 3.

findings.title: The project's creator never has peers: peer feed, overlap warnings and handoffs work one way only
findings.requirement: F.6, F.7, E.5 (send handoff message to peer), F.2
findings.what_a_person_meets: Ada creates a project and Bob's agent works on it. Ada's agent's brief says nothing about Bob, her Overview has no Peers section, her agent never warns Bob or skips his tasks, and Bob never gets a handoff from her. Bob's side sees Ada. After Ada shares the project with Bob (the only sharing control), nothing changes for her.
findings.evidence: packages/runtime/src/daemon/create-project.ts:64 writes `settings: { members: [deps.agent.id] }`. defaultPeers (packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:3143-3165) returns members minus self when members is non-empty, so the creator's list is always []. No code adds a member: grep finds `members` written only in create-project.ts. `shared_with` (packages/commands/src/commands/settings.ts:238-246) does not touch members. Bench: Ada's session events `peers.feed {"peers":[]}`, Bob's `peers.feed` lists Ada's agent (p4.out). The DB message rows hold one handoff, Bob's agent to Ada's, requires_ack, and none the other way. After settings.set shared_with=[Bob], GET /projects/:id/peers on Ada is still [] (probe p5). Screenshot: /tmp/frbench/collab/tests/benches/ada/steps/02-ada-project-overview.png has no Peers section; bob/steps/02-bob-project-overview.png has one. The tests seed members directly: packages/runtime/test/daemon.test.ts:382-392 (a second agent of the same human), packages/capabilities/test/phase2-gate.integration.test.ts:247, tests/e2e/src/scenario-world.ts:892.
findings.expected: Tests that start from the person's path, never from a patched `settings.members`: POST /projects on A's daemon, share through the app's sharing control, then sessions on both. Assert both peer feeds name the other, overlap warnings go both ways, a handoff goes A to B and B to A, and both Overviews show Peers. Rewrite the daemon.test.ts F.6 case and the phase 2 gate to create the project and its sharing the way the app does.
findings.fix_hint: Let sharing (or joining) add the collaborator's principal agent to `settings.members`, or have defaultPeers use members ∪ agents of `shared_with` humans ∪ touched agents.

findings.title: No person-facing way to set up collaboration: no shared-store step, no share-with-a-person control
findings.requirement: F (collaboration as a whole), user-guide promise (docs/user-guide.md:12-14), validation rule 6 (every person-facing step can be done by the person)
findings.what_a_person_meets: The owner, a non-developer on Windows, cannot find how to let a collaborator's Forerunner work on their project. The setup assistant never asks for a shared store. The setup guide's shared state section is about pairing a phone (it sets FORERUNNER_STATE_API_URL, not the database the agents share). Sharing a project means typing a JSON array of the other person's internal human id under Settings, Advanced, and the confirmation reads back a raw UUID.

Sharing: settings.ts:238-246 (`shared_with`, z.array(z.string()), "Human ids"), edited through SettingsPage parseLoose JSON (apps/ui/src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx:195-210). Bench readback (probe p5): "Set who the project is shared with for Shared site to [\"01a19dff-94de-7250-ac49-bc786d78714c\"]? Confirm in the app on a paired device." I could set up the second install only by hand-writing config.json with humanEmail.
findings.expected: (a) A UI test plus a real-daemon case for a person-level sharing control: share by email or name, the confirmation names the person in words, and the collaborator's app then lists the project. (b) A setup-assistant test for joining a shared store (address plus the person's email), asserting the install binds to a new or own human. (c) The two-person bench journey (T-15) and the phase F live journey (T-16), which may only use what a person can click or type.
findings.fix_hint: Decide the person's path to join and share (an ADR), then build it before any collaboration test can be meaningful at the person's boundary.

findings.title: A second install with no email silently becomes the first person; once a second person joins, the first person's install refuses to start
findings.requirement: F.1 (inbox per agent and human), F.4 (claims per agent), S.10, ADR 0082 identity
findings.what_a_person_meets: (1) Bob points his install at the shared store as for the first PC (no email: the app never asks). His Forerunner starts as Ada, with the same human and the same agent, so claims cannot tell the two PCs apart and Ada's Inbox becomes his. (2) Once Bob joins properly with an email, Ada's next start fails: "the state store holds 2 humans and this install names none; set the environment variable FORERUNNER_HUMAN ...".

Bench: Bob's first start logged `install identity {"humanId":"01a19dfe-ba2a-…","source":"only"}`, Ada's id (/tmp/frbench/collab/tests/benches/bob/daemon.log:7 of that start; the DB then held 1 human and 1 principal agent). Lockout: Ada's daemon bound at 20:41 with no config.json, so nothing was recorded; compose.ts:1342-1345 records only when config.json already exists (wizard.ts:186-197). The setup assistant's "Set up later" wrote config.json at 20:44 with no humanId (setupAcknowledgedAt only). Assert A binds to its own human. (2) Install B starts with no selector on a store holding A. Assert it does not bind to A without the person saying so (a refusal or question in words), or record a test-approved design decision.
findings.fix_hint: Record the bound humanId even when config.json does not exist yet (create it), and make the setup assistant keep it. Ask the person before binding to an existing human on a shared store.

findings.title: The daemon applies no ownership check on a shared store: another person's unshared project, tasks and session notes are readable and writable
findings.requirement: S.10 ("Shared means project data only"), ADR 0041 ownership note in packages/commands/src/ownership.ts:1-8, state-service parity ("a device sees only sessions of its own human's agents")
findings.what_a_person_meets: Before Ada shares anything, Bob's app lists Ada's project. No owner check on server.ts:928 (GET /projects/:id), :1025-1027 (POST /projects/:id/tasks), :1382 (POST /sessions), :1453-1455 (GET /sessions/:id), /sessions/:id/events, or /projects/:id/peers (:1766-1779). findings.title: A shared project without a repository has no shared code: each PC works in its own folder and both say everything is done
findings.requirement: F.5 (code only via branches and PRs), design "Your files", validation rule 1

Bob's index.html is a fresh 13-line "Hello" page with no stylesheet or script. Ada's has the real page but not Bob's docs/usage.md or header logo. Both Home screens say "Done: all 6 tasks. Your files: <own path>". Bob's Overview lists "Changed by the last session: index.html, notes/contact.md": Ada's session's files, which are not in his folder.

In every case the files of every done task are reachable from both PCs, and "Last result" and "Changed by the last session" name only files the viewer can open.

findings.title: One desktop does not see the other's changes until a reload (no realtime or polling between two desktops)

findings.what_a_person_meets: Ada has her project's Tasks tab open. Bob adds a task, and 20 seconds later Ada's screen still does not show it. It appears only after she reloads. Messages, claims and session changes made by the other PC behave the same way.

Bench /tmp/frbench/collab/tests/probe ui2.cjs: {beforeHas:false, bobAdd:201, afterHasWithoutReload:false, afterReloadHas:true}. Screenshots ada/steps/04-…, 05-ada-tasks-20s-after-bob-added-no-reload.png, 06-…-after-reload.png. findings.summary: I tested the collaboration module on a bench: two real daemons using the stand-in model on one private Postgres 16 store. Claims between installs that are both online still work: Bob's agent found Ada's claim, sent her a message and moved on. The rest of the module fails for real people, in six major ways. (1) A project only ever lists its creator as a member, so the two sides are lopsided: the creator's agent never sees or hands off to the collaborator, and the collaborator can run sessions on the project but is refused its Docs. (2) A second PC that joins without naming its person silently becomes the first person, with her agent, her inbox and her monthly cap. Joining is possible only from the command line. (3) A project without a repository ends up split between the two PCs: every task is done, but neither PC has all the work. (4) If an agent loses its claim during a run, nothing notices. The run finishes, marks the task done and wipes the other agent's claim. (5) The peer feed ignores pull requests that were accepted but not yet merged. With the owner's new "you press Merge" default, that is every pull request. (6) Every person sees and can run every project and session on the shared store. There is also no channel at all between installs that do not share a store, which is the owner's likely setup. The code that talks to GitHub has no way to edit a comment, pin or lock an issue, or see who wrote a comment, and the test stand-in for GitHub lacks these too. The standard doc set still creates an untrue docs/status.md and has no guide. Requirements F.1 to F.7 are marked done, but no test runs two real daemons on Postgres. The notes give the design: the status issue as the shared noticeboard across stores, and AGENTS.md plus a one-line CLAUDE.md as the standard repository guide. Evidence is in /tmp/frbench/collab/design/evidence.txt and /tmp/frbench/collab/design/{ada,bob,bobnaive}/daemon.log. All processes I started were stopped by PID and the bench homes and Postgres data were deleted. Disk stays at 11 GB free.
